technology_and_technique.summary: Simulation enables deliberate practice in a low-risk environment and is reported to expedite acquisition of basic bronchoscopic skills, improve learner confidence, and reduce procedural time. A recent meta-analysis found positive effects of simulation on learning, though heterogeneity in design and assessment limited definitive conclusions. No specific diagnostic yield percentages or patient safety outcomes are reported.

High-fidelity simulation (animal models, cadaver labs) offers greater realism and immersion than low-fidelity or virtual reality simulators but comes with higher cost, lower availability, and ethical considerations. Limited evidence suggests high-fidelity training may provide superior learning gains for novice trainees; longer-term studies are needed to confirm. No comparative diagnostic yield or procedural safety data are provided.

technology_and_technique.topic: Educational strategies to improve procedural performance
technology_and_technique.summary: Use of simulation, deliberate practice, and movement toward mastery-based assessments are highlighted. Future research priorities include optimizing feedback for skill retention and demonstrating transfer of simulation-acquired skills to patient care. No quantitative performance or safety statistics are provided.

technology_and_technique.topic: Scope of interventional pulmonology diagnostic techniques
technology_and_technique.summary: Training focuses on minimally invasive diagnosis and management of lung cancer, pleural disease, benign airway disease, and central airway obstruction with specialized airway and pleural procedures. The chapter does not provide diagnostic yield percentages, comparative effectiveness against other modalities, or patient selection criteria.

technology_and_technique.topic: Assessment framework related to procedural competence
technology_and_technique.summary: Knowledge-based requirements are assessed via biannual in-service exams and a postfellowship board certification exam. While relevant to ensuring procedural quality, the chapter does not include modality-specific diagnostic yields or safety outcomes.

Abstract 
Interventional pulmonary (IP) and advanced bronchos-
copy training occurs in various stages of a physician 
career

Competency had traditionally been developed in 
formal fellowship training with mastery developing over 
the entire career

With the rapid rate of new procedures, 
knowledge and procedures learned in fellowship may 
become obsolete requiring competency developed as a 
part of continuing medical education
